title: veyq node kinds of one owner
description: The facts of the node kinds one owner answers for (ADR 0079 decision 3): core's own `FOLDER` (`core.json`) and each application's kinds (`<application>.json`, the file named for the application's id, its entry of contracts/platform/capabilities.json). Both clients answer the same facts by hand in their own language — the backend through its seams (`NodeKindRules`, `ShareRoots`, `GuestNodeRules`, `GuestCreatableKinds`, `WriteOnlyGuestKinds`), the web through its registry and its rights functions — and each holds its answers to this file in a test: the backend's `KindsContractTest` (src/backend/src/test/kotlin/me/raddatz/veyq/app/), which asks every deployed bean and finds every kind constant of the compiled code in a file, and the web's `kindsContract.test.ts` (src/web/src/), which asks the registry and each application's rights function. So the two cannot drift apart without one of them going red, and a new kind is written down here before either side takes it. The server stays the authority: the web's placement is a hint its move dialog offers by, the server's `illegal_structure` the answer. A file records what is built; changing a fact here changes it on both sides or neither test is green.

owner.description: `core`, or the application's id (`memories`, `depot`, `expenses`): the file's name without `.json`. A kind of `core` belongs to no application and is never switched off; an application's kind answers its id as `NodeKindRules.applicationOf` on the backend and `registry.applicationOf` on the web, and its rules live in that application's code.

kinds.description: Each kind this owner answers for, by its wire token (`_common` `NodeKind`). A kind appears in exactly one file.

placement.description: Where a node of the kind may live: the backend's `NodeKindRules.parentAllows` (`illegal_structure` elsewhere), the web's `KindDescriptor.placement` (core's move dialog). A kind no `parents` entry of any kind names takes no placed child.

parents.description: Directly in a node of each of these kinds, and of no other.

cover.description: It carries a cover in core's `COVER` slot: the backend's `NodeKindRules.takesCover`, the web's `KindDescriptor.cover`.

createNeeds.description: The capability id (contracts/platform/capabilities.json) creating a node of the kind needs, or null: the backend's `NodeKindRules.capabilityToCreate` (`capability_disabled`), the web's create entry, which a member with that leaf off is not offered.

shareRoles.description: The roles a link rooted at a node of the kind may have (`ShareRole`; empty: it roots no link): the backend's `ShareRoots`, the web's share dialog (`KindDescriptor.shareDialog`, present exactly when this is not empty), its rights function's `share` (READ), `shareContribute` (READ_WRITE) and `shareUpload` (WRITE_ONLY) for a member with every leaf on, and its drop page (`app.shareBody`, claimed exactly for a WRITE_ONLY root).

guest.description: What a link's guest may do with the tree around a node of the kind (ADR 0080 decisions 6 and 11).

creatableInFolder.description: A `READ_WRITE` guest of a folder link may create a node of the kind inside a `FOLDER`: core's `FolderGuestNodeRules` for `FOLDER`, an application's `GuestCreatableKinds` for its own kinds on the backend; on the web, a level menu entry of the kind (or core's folder create) that such a guest is offered.

container.description: Inside a node of the kind a `READ_WRITE` guest moves any kind in and out, renames any kind and creates the `creatableInFolder` kinds — the one guest container shape built, a `FOLDER`'s (`GuestNodeRules`); false: no guest tree operation inside it. On the web core's `nodeRights` lets such a guest move only what a container lets out.

writeOnlyCreates.description: The kinds a `WRITE_ONLY` guest of a link rooted at a node of the kind may create inside its own identity folder (`WriteOnlyGuestKinds`); empty: none. Backend only: the web's drop page (`app.shareBody`) is the one place such a guest creates, and it is the application's own.
